title: Radio Emission from the Magnetically Active M Dwarf UV Ceti from 1 to 105 GHz
question: What are the radio emission components (flares, auroral ECME, persistent) of UV Ceti across 1–105 GHz, and which emission mechanisms explain them given its strong large-scale field?

data.bands: VLA L, S, C, Ku, K, Ka; ALMA band 3

what.value: Orbital parameters and masses of the binary; stellar radius 0.159±0.006 Rsun

evidence.quote: using masses and orbital parameters from (cite: Kervella2016) as input to the ephemeris calculator tool

what.value: Eight earlier VLA spectra for comparison

evidence.quote: Figure [3](#fig:flux) also shows eight other VLA observations, from (cite: gudelbenz1996radiospectra) and (cite: Gudel1989).
Since UV Ceti rotates with a period of 5.45 hours (cite: Barnes2016)

recipe.method: tclean images; Gaussian fit and peak pixel flux with off-source RMS
Shift phase center with fixvis, subtract other sources' model, average visibilities over channels, spws and baselines; ALMA light curve from five per-scan images

recipe.goal: Astrometric identification of the emitting binary component
recipe.method: Gaussian position fits compared to Gaia-based predicted positions of UV and BL Ceti
Image sidebands separately; power law fit; uncertainties by Monte Carlo propagation
Brightness temperature assuming source size equal to stellar disk; compare cyclotron harmonic field strengths with dipole field
assumptions: Emitting region equals stellar disk; dipole field 2 kG at pole; radius 0.159 Rsun

evidence.quote: The millimeter emission has a spectral index $-0.81\pm0.36$
UV Ceti gradually brightened by 36% during the ALMA observation

answer_key.quantity: ALMA position offset from UV Ceti

evidence.quote: $0.09\pm0.41$ arcseconds from the expected position of UV Ceti
the flux density implies a brightness temperature of $6.5\times 10^5$ K

answer_key.quantity: K band spectral index Jan 8 flare

evidence.quote: the K band emission from UV Ceti has a spectral index $0.56\pm0.17$

not_stated_but_needed: tclean cell size, image size, niter, thresholds and masks
ALMA field and spectral-window selection and any channel averaging
Method for flux density at each ALMA scan, and Monte Carlo details for the spectral index
Stellar disk size and distance used for the brightness temperatures
missing_for_reproduction: Flux extraction details for ALMA per-scan images
score_reason: Public archival data and simple workflow, but imaging parameters and CASA version are missing.
rediscovery_reason: Public data, stated calibrators and weighting, numeric results such as the ALMA spectral index and 36% brightening.
